sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 6357.6 ± 30.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by labeling intact (non-permeabilized) cells with membrane-impermeable dye CA-sulfo646 (HA-Halo constructs) and CLIP-surface 547 (FLAG-CLIP constructs); single-molecule pull-down experiments detected surface receptor. No cAMP or radioligand binding result is stated in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: MC3R is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–43 as extracellular and TM1 begins at residue 44, so the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag. The papers replace nothing in MC3R itself: an exogenous signal sequence is added upstream, which is cleaved post-translationally, leaving the HA/FLAG + Halo/SNAP/CLIP module at the extracellular face immediately before MC3R residue 1 (M). Python verification confirms residue 1 = M and TM1 starts at residue 44, giving 43 residues of extracellular space—well clear of the >=3-residue TM boundary constraint. Because no paper states a residue number for the junction (only the construct architecture), position_evidence is topology_derived: with a single extracellular terminus, the junction is uniquely determined. ss-HA-Halo-MC3R and ss-HA-SNAP-MC3R constructs built with exogenous signal sequence (MVLLLILSVLLLKEDVRG), linker (SAQSTR), HA tag (YPYDVPDYA), linker (TRGSGS), Halo or SNAP tag, linker (RS), then full-length human MC3R gene; expressed in transfected cells and labeled with membrane-impermeable dyes on intact non-permeabilized cells, confirming surface display. The same N-terminal architecture is independently used in PMC7618510, PMC11580913, PMC12485739 (L1–L10), and a 3xHA variant in PMC3465685 (L11) and SNAP-only variant in PMC13215352 (L12).

sources.claim: For ss-HA-Halo-GPCR and ss-HA-SNAP-GPCR, plasmids were constructed as follows: signal sequence (MVLLLILSVLLLKEDVRG), linker (SAQSTR), HA tag (YPYDVPDYA), linker (TRGSGS), Halo or SNAP tag, linker (RS), GPCR or MRAP2 gene.

literature_notes: All twelve qualifying ledger lines (L1–L12) converge on the same N-terminal prepend site (insert_after_residue=0). L2 and L3 are the most explicit, giving the exact exogenous signal sequence and linker architecture. L8 and L9 provide the strongest surface-display validation (membrane-impermeable dye labeling on intact cells; single-molecule imaging). L11 (3xHA-MC3R, PMC3465685) and L12 (SNAP-MC3R, PMC13215352) are independent constructs at the same junction. No ledger line supports any internal loop insertion (ECL1, ECL2, ECL3) for MC3R. L13 describes a C-terminal LgBiT fusion used for cryo-EM stabilization; the C-terminus (residues 302–323) is intracellular per the topology landmarks and is recorded in other_positions. ECL2 (182–186) and ECL3 (269–278) are very short (5 and 10 residues respectively) and contain cysteines (C274, C276 in ECL3) that are likely involved in disulfide bonds; no ledger line supports insertion there in any case.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT subunit fused at the C-terminus of full-length MC3R via a 15-aa linker for NanoBiT tethering to stabilize the MC3R–Gs complex for cryo-EM; residue 323 (G) falls within the intracellular C-terminal region (302–323) per topology landmarks.
